findings.title: Login-cache invalidation compares an organization-aware original with a raw updated model
findings.body: update() obtains the original through getById(), which returns createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(): its isEnabled() also returns false when the linked organization is disabled. The updated model passed by callers is normally the raw model. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() therefore evaluates LoginFilter.ENABLED against different semantics for the two models. For example, for an enabled public broker in a disabled organization whose BROKER_PUBLIC is changed from true to false, the wrapped original already fails the login predicate because isEnabled() is false, and the raw updated model also fails it because it is no longer public, so both are treated as 'not a login IdP' and no invalidation is registered. The stale cached getForLogin list can then expose the now-private broker after the organization is re-enabled. The original's underlying IdP fields, not the organization-aware isEnabled(), must be used for this comparison.

findings.title: New login predicate can NPE on an IdP model with null config
findings.body: getLoginPredicate() now unconditionally calls idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) for every organization-linked IdP. IdentityProviderModel.setConfig() allows the config map to be replaced, including with null, and previously this predicate only called simple boolean getters. The Infinispan provider now invokes this predicate from create(), update(), and remove() invalidation handling, so an org-linked model with a null config can fail those operations with a NullPointerException instead of being created, updated, or removed. The predicate should treat a null config as not public.

findings.title: New test cleanup removes a literal alias instead of the created IdPs
findings.body: Each loop iteration creates an IdP aliased "idp-alias-" + i but registers cleanup as testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove, using the literal string "alias" rather than the created alias (the same mistake is repeated for idp-alias-20 at line 425). Cleanup therefore does not remove the twenty created providers and may attempt to remove a non-existent provider, leaving state that can pollute subsequent tests using the shared test realm and mask or cause cache-count failures.
